places.name: The Held Breath
sources: module 20 §12.3b hard-to-reach types (underwater grottoes, air pockets, flooded cellars)
uesp:Lore:Argonian (amphibious physiology; the crossing is priced around held breath)

why.founding: A maintained air pocket on a flooded root route, kept so the crossing is survivable.
why.siteAdvantages: The midpoint of the longest flooded branch in the region.
why.occupantsMotive: Unstaffed; it is maintained by whoever passes, on an interior custom that anyone using the shelter repairs it before leaving.
why.pressures: The seal leaks and the pocket is smaller each decade. The Waykeepers who could reseal it will not work outside a paid line.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing it makes the flooded route impassable. Every crossing then goes by the long root gallery, a day longer and a band of danger worse.

preferences: water relation: fully enclosed by water
neighbours: inside a drowned or flooded place

places.traversalFallback: walk the surface route (two days, D5 ground)

vibe.palette: root-brown lit by a single carried lamp, silver bubbles pinned under the ceiling, the tally scars pale against dark bark, a dropped flower gone black at the dive line
vibe.materials: the seal is old resin poured thin and cracking at the rim; the bubble ceiling is bare root with no lashing at all; the tally marks are cut, not painted, four hundred deep; dry stores wedged into a natural root shelf
vibe.signatureFeature: A dry bubble the size of a room, thirty metres down a flooded gallery, with a tally cut into the root, one mark for each rest taken.
vibe.condition: the seal thinner every year; the Waykeepers have not been paid to reseal it
vibe.approach: The dive to it is one held breath from the last air.
vibe.senses: held breath and the pop of a fresh air pocket breaking the surface; cold water pressing at the ankles even when the chest is dry; the ceiling drips on a slow count, which divers use to time the next dive

places.name: Alten Markmont
sources: Lore:Alten Markmont (Arena gazetteer); Lore:East Empire Company

why.founding: An outsider-facing trading station built where the southern water route met the Helstrom approach; the alten- prefix marks it as never Argonian.
why.siteAdvantages: A landing on deep-enough water at the last point outsiders were tolerated.
why.occupantsMotive: A skeleton staff of two factors and whoever is sheltering in the warehouses. The two factors are paid a retainer by a company that no longer trades here, on the theory that a lapsed post is cheaper to hold than to re-license.
why.pressures: The interior tolerates it but does not need it. The trade it was built for stopped. The warehouses now shelter people the factors are not allowed to register.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single busy season would refill it. The Helstrom assembly has decided there will not be one.

preferences: water relation: on a navigable route inland
neighbours: too far inland for its own logistics

places.name: Thousand-Chimes
sources: Lore:Bright-Throat Village; Lore:Argonian (jewellery, guarded weaving secrets)

why.founding: A craft village that makes the bone and tin chimes through which half the province listens to its Hist.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside a hero Hist whose wind is reliable. The chimes are tuned against the tree that will hang them.
why.occupantsMotive: Chime-makers whose tuning is a religious qualification, not a trade skill. Tuning is examined and licensed by the tree-minders, so a maker who loses the qualification loses the craft and the village at once.
why.pressures: Cheap cast chimes from the cities are undercutting them and, they say, mistranslating the trees. The tree-minders have declined to rule on that for six years.
why.wouldChangeIf: A ruling that cast chimes are valid would end the village's authority. The coastal foundries would take the province's trade within a decade.

preferences: water relation: within poling reach of a trade channel, though the tuning tree sets the site
neighbours: on a trade water; brokers between neighbours

notableNpcSlots: the chime-maker
the deelith who teaches the trade

places.name: The Under-Ring

why.founding: Barsaebic Ayleid works that predate the interior tribes' own works and go down rather than up.
why.siteAdvantages: Whatever the Ayleids wanted here is underground now, in rings that fill from beneath every wet season and drain again.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing that talks. The lower rings are dry, which is why animals den in them.
why.pressures: Antiquarians want in but the interior tribes have no stake either way. Two licensed parties have gone down; neither came back up.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dig licence from anywhere would open it. The Helstrom assembly would then have to decide whether Ayleid stone falls under the Duskfall taboo.

preferences: water relation: dry, elevated
neighbours: in the north and west, where the Barsaebic Ayleids went

places.name: Long-Stride

why.founding: The keepers bred lizard-steeds on this rise for two generations before a wet season flooded the schooling paddock and let the breeding stock loose.
why.siteAdvantages: The same firm rise and soft-ground paddock that once suited training now suits a wamasu denned in the flooded pens.
why.occupantsMotive: The wamasu that took the paddock has no reason to leave water this good and this undisturbed.
why.pressures: Porters who once bought steeds here now route wide around the pens. The loss has driven up prices on every interior road.
why.wouldChangeIf: Killing or driving off the wamasu would leave the pens open for breeding again, but there has been no attempt since the keepers scattered.

preferences: water relation: penned water separated from open channel
neighbours: supplies mounts or protection to a district

notableNpcSlots: the keeper who names every animal
the ka-deelith who breaks them

places.name: The Staying Stone
sources: Lore:Wamasu (Haynekhtnamet of Shadowfen received offerings to stop seasonal flooding)

why.founding: A shrine where offerings are made to hold back the flood, maintained by four villages jointly.
why.siteAdvantages: The pinch point where the flood enters this basin.
why.occupantsMotive: Unoccupied. Four villages take turns. The turn order is older than any of their current naheesh.
why.pressures: The floods have not obeyed for three years and the villages are blaming each other, chiefly the one whose turn fell in the worst year.
why.wouldChangeIf: One more bad year and the shrine will be abandoned or rebuilt bigger. Either decision breaks the four-village compact, which is the district's only joint institution.

preferences: water relation: facing the creature's water
neighbours: between a village and a lair

notableNpcSlots: the offering-keeper

vibe.palette: floodwater brown against green banks, offerings pale on dark stone, tin chime frames catching grey light, moss climbing the ledges nearest the water
vibe.materials: stone ledges set four abreast, one per village; roof beams gone since the last storm and left bare; rope ties replaced only by whichever village's turn it is; paint renewed yearly over the old marks

vibe.condition: patched only by whichever village's turn falls due
vibe.approach: A stone in the water with fresh and rotted offerings side by side.
vibe.senses: standing water underfoot at every tide; rot on the oldest offerings, sweetness on the newest; cold stone through wet feet; gulls working the shallows for scraps

places.name: Keeps-the-Egg
sources: Lore:Hist (a settlement without a Hist is always political)

why.founding: Their Hist was killed in the Imperial century; the tribe recovered the Mnemic Egg and organised itself around keeping it.
why.siteAdvantages: They did not move. The dead trunk is still the centre of the village and the Egg is kept inside it.
why.occupantsMotive: Custodians of a memory none of them can currently read.
why.pressures: Three other tribes claim a share of the Egg. One has offered to buy it, publicly, so that refusing would look like hoarding.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reading the Egg, which the main quest's archivists could, would resolve or destroy them. Each claimant tribe has decided which outcome it wants.

preferences: water relation: as a hist-village
neighbours: neighbours argue about taking them in

notableNpcSlots: the egg-tender who kept the log
the naheesh who will not have the clutch spoken of

vibe.silhouette: a dead trunk still standing at the centre, kept, not cleared
vibe.palette: bone-pale heartwood scaffolding against grey bark, the Egg's chamber lit orange from inside, dust settled thick on the log shelf, dulled iron on the naheesh's staff
vibe.materials: the dead trunk is propped with green-cut props still weeping sap at the driven ends; the Egg's chamber is walled with fitted bark tile, no gaps; the scaffold ladders are lashed fresh each season and left rough underfoot

places.name: The Lit Fen
sources: Lore:Wamasu (luminescent organs); Lore:Guar (Glowgill); module 55 (night is authored world state, so night-only places are legitimate)

why.founding: A fen where the water itself lights at night from Hist-flower fall.
why.siteAdvantages: Still water directly downstream of a hero Hist's grove.
why.occupantsMotive: Unkept. The villages come once a year, on a night fixed by the Tsoko stones. They come in numbers because of what waits in the deep channel.
why.pressures: It only lights while the tree above flowers. This year the light came late and stopped early.
why.wouldChangeIf: The tree failing would put the fen out. The district would see the fen go dark weeks before the grove announced anything.

preferences: water relation: still or tidal water, undisturbed
neighbours: known and visited; a destination, not a secret

vibe.materials: no structure here beyond root shelf and silt bank; a single old shrine post driven at the shallow end; a fallen limb wedged across for a crossing; bare mud banked where the last flood pushed it

places.name: The Raw Hold
sources: Lore:Blackrose Prison (the Blackguards' heirs, prison-descended three generations)

why.founding: A Blackguard crew hiding in the interior because nowhere else will have them.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep, off every route, with one boat exit.
why.occupantsMotive: Criminals with no ledger and no discipline, most of them three generations out of Blackrose and unable to work anywhere their descent is known.
why.pressures: They cannot resupply and are starting to raid villages they need. Raiding the villages they depend on has ended other crews the same way.
why.wouldChangeIf: A village retaliation would finish them within a year. The interior tribes have already agreed among themselves which village would lead it.

preferences: water relation: boat access, concealed
neighbours: answers to a reoccupied prison

places.name: Many-Ways
sources: Lore:Murkmire (platforms ascending from ground to hover above water)

why.founding: A village that grew as a junction of walkways rather than around a centre.
why.siteAdvantages: Where four routes over soft ground have to meet, because there is nowhere else to put them. The junction is the village's whole capital.
why.occupantsMotive: Walkway-keepers who charge for maintenance and argue about who owes what.
why.pressures: The walkways cost more to keep than the village earns. The keepers have begun charging tolls the tribes using the arms consider extortion.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing one arm of the junction would strand a whole tribe's route. That tribe has started surveying its own alternative rather than keep paying.

places.name: The Carriers' Rest

vibe.silhouette: terraced monumental massing with smoke and washing on it
vibe.palette: green-grey terraces kept deliberately clear of growth, amber lamplight in the stair mouths after dark, a single red flower on the one tree left inside the walls, black wet stone underfoot
vibe.materials: xanmeer stone maintained rather than replaced, against the objections of neighbouring tribes; trained root binding the newer additions to the old; withy and flint-vine lashing the hoardings in place; working vakka mechanisms set into the terrace walls
vibe.signatureFeature: Working xanmeer traps guarding a doorway with laundry hung across it.
vibe.condition: lived in and maintained daily, its traps left running and occasionally fatal
vibe.approach: The terraces break the canopy and the smoke comes out of them.
vibe.senses: stone treads answering underfoot at every terrace; laundry snapping in the wind across a trap doorway; a mechanism resetting somewhere below with a distant clunk; cooking smoke drifting out across the walls

places.whySiteWon: summit in firm lowland (danger band 4), 710 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, remote.

playerPurpose.hook: Working xanmeer traps guard a doorway with the laundry hung across it. The tribe living inside calls that maintenance.

loot.provenance: a fort that has never been taken
